domain: Genomic Variant Analysis & Petabyte DNA Sequencing
title: $18.4M Population-Scale WGS Platform for 2.5PB Biobank Cohort
executive_summary: Acme Genomics Cloud proposes a $18.4M three-year turnkey platform to process and archive 2.5 petabytes of whole-genome data for a national biobank. Technical review reveals critical gaps between sales guarantees on availability, turnaround, and hot storage versus engineered limits on throughput, maintenance downtime, and tiered lifecycle costs.

proposal_document.title: Commercial Proposal v1.0
proposal_document.text: Acme Genomics Cloud proposes a turnkey 2.5-petabyte sequencing platform to process 10,000 whole genomes per day with guaranteed 24-hour turnaround from FASTQ to annotated VCF. We guarantee 99.99% pipeline availability with zero-downtime variant calling and immutable audit trails for every pipeline run. All raw FASTQ and aligned BAM files will be retained in hot NVMe storage for 7 years at no additional cost. We also include unlimited free reprocessing of historical cohorts using updated GATK best-practice runbooks, with enterprise-grade HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance included by default.

technical_specification.title: Technical Architecture Spec v4.2
technical_specification.text: The production variant-calling cluster is engineered for 99.5% monthly availability excluding scheduled maintenance windows every Sunday 02:00-06:00 UTC during which pipeline execution is paused. Maximum sustained throughput is 4,000 30x whole genomes per day with a standard 72-hour turnaround from FASTQ ingestion to annotated VCF under nominal load. Storage lifecycle policy retains raw FASTQ and BAM files in hot NVMe tier for 90 days, after which data is automatically tiered to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for up to 7 years; retrieval from archive requires 12-48 hours and incurs egress fees. Pipeline runbooks are version-locked as immutable Docker images, requiring formal change request and revalidation for any GATK version update, and encryption at rest uses AES-256 with HIPAA-eligible controls pending customer-owned key configuration.

commitments.proposal_quote: We guarantee 99.99% pipeline availability with zero-downtime variant calling and immutable audit trails for every pipeline run.
commitments.spec_quote: The production variant-calling cluster is engineered for 99.5% monthly availability excluding scheduled maintenance windows every Sunday 02:00-06:00 UTC during which pipeline execution is paused.
commitments.explanation: Proposal promises 99.99% with zero downtime, while spec explicitly allows 4 hours of weekly paused execution and only commits to 99.5% excluding that window.

commitments.claim: Unlimited free reprocessing with updated GATK runbooks
commitments.proposal_quote: We also include unlimited free reprocessing of historical cohorts using updated GATK best-practice runbooks
commitments.explanation: Spec never mentions free or unlimited reprocessing; it states runbooks are version-locked and require formal change request and revalidation for any GATK update, implying scoped, chargeable work.

commitments.claim: Enterprise-grade HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance included by default
commitments.proposal_quote: with enterprise-grade HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance included by default.
commitments.spec_quote: encryption at rest uses AES-256 with HIPAA-eligible controls pending customer-owned key configuration.
commitments.explanation: Spec qualifies compliance as HIPAA-eligible and pending customer-owned key configuration with no mention of SOC 2, leaving scope, shared responsibility, and audit readiness uncertain.

commitments.claim: 7-year retention of FASTQ and BAM files
commitments.proposal_quote: All raw FASTQ and aligned BAM files will be retained in hot NVMe storage for 7 years at no additional cost.
commitments.spec_quote: after which data is automatically tiered to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for up to 7 years
commitments.explanation: Spec confirms the 7-year retention duration for FASTQ and BAM data, even though storage tier and retrieval cost differ from the hot-storage, no-fee promise.
